source: Five user photographs of the Passaporte para Português glossary: pages 126, 128, 130, 132 and 134, including readable following-page fragments
normalization_notes: Manually transcribe main pages 126, 128, 130, 132 and 134 and fully readable rows from following-page fragments. Do not infer unphotographed rows.
Exclude running publisher text, headings and page numbers; printed references are source references, not CEFR levels.
Use lowercase NFC individual words; remove punctuation and trailing gender articles, retaining articles and prepositions occurring within expressions.

Separate attached pronouns: calar-se, chamar-se, despachar-se, despedir-se, despir-se, divertir-se, encontrar-se and ir-se become verb plus se. Preserve the pronominal constructions in source context.
Keep lexical hyphens in cor-de-rosa; cor de laranja remains three individual words.
Expand com/de certeza and estar/fazer calor into their components. The o/a annotations on chefe and cliente use one Portuguese spelling.
Preserve context words in parentheses, including médica, bancária, simples and musical/transport expressions; translate each word individually.
Split holiday names into individual words and preserve the original capitalized names in source JSON.
Several rows at page bottoms and main-page edges overlap earlier photo batches; retain source occurrences and deduplicate against SQLite.

dictionary_checks.note: Verified standalone happen sense and separate se calhar expression meaning maybe.
Verified groups of ten; translated as tens rather than literally copying the German Dutzende (dozens).

translation_notes: Dezenas means tens/groups of ten. The source German Dutzende is retained but not used as the precise numerical translation.
Constipado means having a cold in European Portuguese; it does not mean constipated.
Empurre is the command push. Puxe from the earlier batch means pull.
Calhar is translated as a verb; maybe belongs to the full expression se calhar, retained in source JSON.
Calçado is footwear, and calçar means to put on footwear. Cor-de-rosa remains a single lexical compound.
Patrício and Valentim are translated as personal names in the photographed saint-day expressions, not as the entire holiday names.
São is saint before male names in the source; the common are form of ser is also included and identified.
Direito combines the photographed direction and law senses in one new entry. Existing entrada already covers both entrance and starter.
Reflexive constructions retain se as a separate word. Additional construction-specific meanings for old verbs remain in JSON rather than replacing old translations.
Câmara municipal, chapéu de chuva, cinto de segurança and holiday names remain whole expressions in JSON while their individual words are imported.
Escreve is a form meaning writes/write; it is not assigned the whole question translation of Como se escreve?.
Clipped following-page rows are documented; those pages were already imported from complete photos in earlier batches.
New words start at mastery 0. Existing IDs, translations, levels and learning history are preserved.
